ss-delta 0.4.0 runs on Android: the app builds the game on the device itself, from your own dump, with no PC. On every platform it also takes the Japanese Voice-over Pack and rePatch mods such as the Undub patch, shows Xbox button labels and can skip the intro logos.

## Downloads

| System | Download | Start |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11, x64 | `ss-delta-v0.4.0-windows.zip` | `ss-delta.exe` |
| Linux x64, Steam Deck | `ss-delta-v0.4.0-linux.tar.gz` | `ss-delta.x86_64` |
| macOS 13.3+ on Apple Silicon | `ss-delta-v0.4.0-macos.tar.gz` | `Soul Sacrifice Delta.app` |
| Android 9+, 64-bit ARM with Vulkan | `ss-delta-v0.4.0-android.apk` | **ss-delta** (install the APK) |

On a PC, unpack the archive and start the game. The first time, its importer asks for your own dump of Soul Sacrifice Delta (US PCSA00152 or EU PCSF00532, update 1.30), downloads the PS Vita firmware from Sony and a compiler, and builds the game on your computer in a few minutes. From then on the program goes straight to the game. Nothing of the game is in these downloads. See the [installation guide](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md).

macOS: the app isn't signed by a registered Apple developer, so macOS refuses it the first time. Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click "Open Anyway".

## New

* **Android.** Install the APK and start **ss-delta**. Its setup screen asks for your dump (the NoNpDrm `.zip` or `.vpk`, or the `.pkg` with its licence and the update's `.pkg`), downloads the firmware from Sony, installs the game, and builds its native code on the device: about 15 minutes on a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, with about 10 GB of free space (5 GB of it only while building). Keep the device charging; you can leave the app while it builds. The app carries its own compiler (zig) and Python for this, and nothing leaves the device. Made for Snapdragon handhelds and tested on an AYN Thor, where quests run natively at 60 fps. On Adreno GPUs the game offers to download Turnip, the open-source driver that draws its fog and smoke correctly. On a phone without a gamepad, on-screen controls (the Vita's buttons, D-pad and both sticks, a LOCK toggle for the lock-on so L needn't be held, and a menu button) appear; a finger anywhere else touches the game's own touchscreen, the Black Rite icon stays clear, and they hide while a gamepad is used (size, opacity and On/Off on the settings menu's Controls page). Holding Select opens the settings menu, which on Android leaves out what only a PC has (window, fullscreen, keyboard keys). After an app update the setup builds the native code again by itself, without the dump. A PC that has built the game can also put it on a device: `ss-delta.exe --android` ([Android](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md#android)). The APK is signed with the project's release key, so later versions install over it and keep your saves.
* **The Japanese Voice-over Pack.** The game's separate PSN add-on (the pack for your version: `UP9000-PCSA00152_00-SSS000CVN0000001` for US, `EP9000-PCSF00532_00-SSS000CVN0000001` for EU) installs as an add-on, as a decrypted dump (a NoNpDrm folder or `.zip`) or as its `.pkg` with its `work.bin` or `.rif` beside it. Once the game is built, the pack goes in on its own in seconds, without building again: `ss-delta.exe --dump "<the pack>"` or the importer (`--install`) on a PC, **Add an add-on** (long press on the app's icon) on Android, the Add-ons step in RecompLauncher. Then choose it in the game: Options, Lang/Sub Settings, Voice Language, Japanese.
* **rePatch mods, such as the Undub patch** ([#8](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/8)). The [Undub patch](https://archive.org/details/soul_sacrifice_delta_undub_patch) gives Japanese voices from the very start, also without the pack. Unpack its `.7z` and add the folder that holds `rePatch` (or a `.zip` of it) as an add-on, in the same ways as the pack; for the US or the EU game alike, with no renaming. The mod is kept beside the game in `fs/ux0/rePatch/`, so the game's own files stay as they are, and **Mods (rePatch)** on the settings menu's Game page turns it off.
* **Xbox button labels** (Button prompts on the settings menu's Game page): the game's prompts, its tutorial pictures and the few button symbols in its text show A, B, X, Y, LB, RB, Menu and View instead of the PlayStation symbols, following your gamepad bindings. "As the gamepad" picks Xbox letters for a lettered gamepad and the game's own symbols for a PlayStation pad. It switches while the game runs.
* **Skip intro logos** ([#6](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/6); Skip intro logos on the Game page, off by default): the health warning and the four company logos are skipped, and the game opens on its title screen about 6 seconds after it starts instead of 20.

## Fixed

* **A dump that holds only the update** ([#5](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/issues/5)). Given the 1.30 update's folder alone, the setup downloaded everything and then failed with Vita3K's "Install app before patch". It now stops before the downloads and says what to give it: the NoNpDrm dump's `.zip`, or the folder that holds both `app` and `patch`.
* **The settings menu's pages** no longer run into each other in its tab bar ("MultiplayerNative codeDebug").
* **The settings menu froze** when opened over one of the system's dialogs (the save list, "Do you want to load this saved data?"): it answered no button and the game had to be closed. It now works there, and the dialog carries on once the menu closes.

## Upgrading from 0.3

Unpack 0.4.0 over your game's folder (replace the files), then start it with `--install` and build again from the same dump: saves and settings are kept. Through RecompLauncher this happens by itself. Coming from 0.2, see [Updating](https://github.com/vita-recomps/ss-delta/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md#updating).

SHA-256 and build attestations: see the files attached, and `gh attestation verify`.
